pr_title: mixedversion: run skip-version upgrades when supported
pr_body:
This changes the `mixedversion` framework to randomly perform "skip-version" upgrades when supported. Specifically, v23.1 onwards supports skip-version upgrades, where a single rolling upgrade can be performed to upgrade Cockroach two major releases at a time.

This behaviour is still experimental, and it is necessary to set an environment variable to enable this feature.

Tests that perform logic specific to a certain upgrade path can disable this functionality by using the `DisableSkipVersionUpgrades` option or gating certain steps behind a `helper.IsSkipVersionUpgrade` check.

Fixes: #121957
Epic: none
Release note: None

issue_context.title: roachtest: change mixedversion tests to perform "skip version" upgrades
issue_context.body:
We should make mixedversion tests (like `version-upgrade`) test version skipping, e.g. upgrade from 23.1 directly to 24.1.

PR #106114 was an attempt at this, but it did not get completed.

CC @celiala @rail 

Jira issue: CRDB-37643
comments:
Could someone remind me what are the possible "skip version" scenarios? 

* 23.1 -> 24.1
* 23.2 -> 24.2

Alternatively, would it be valid to say (for now) that every version starting from X (maybe 23.1) can perform a "skip version" upgrade?

cc @celiala

Correct, 23.1 -> 24.1 and 23.2 -> master/24.2 (which is equivalent to saying we can skip starting with 23.1).

This proposed test would try to upgrade from releases with version `clusterversion.MinSupported` to `Latest`.  Equivalently, it could check if `MinSupported < PreviousRelease`, in which case, it would select a predecessor of a predecessor.

I also did a couple of manual runs of `schemachange/mixed-versions` by forcing to skip the penultimate version [1]. It seems the current (upgrade) machinery supports "version skipping", but we still need to add it as an optional feature to the mixed-version framework.

[1] https://github.com/srosenberg/cockroach/commit/ab2b91dc3c0108e79df4bfee46ba91f105dccdc8

I have a draft PR to implement this, but it's not quite ready to be used: master's version is still at 24.1.X, which means a "skip-version" upgrade from master would start from a release in the 23.1 series. However, `master`'s MinSupported was already bumped to 23.2, so that wouldn't work.

We could bump master to 24.2, but then its immediate predecessor would be 24.1, and we don't have any rcs for that release yet.

TLDR: I'll put that PR on pause until we have an rc for 24.1 (_and_ are able to generate fixtures for 24.1, _and_ are able to bump master to 24.2).
Why was this closed? #125869 hasn't merged yet. Reopening.

review_comments: @DarrylWong seems like we're no longer passing the cluster settings when restarting binaries here. I think this is a bug?

Ah yes thank you, that's definitely not correct. Will need to test it out but might be why [change-replicas/mixed-version](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/127106) is failing. Still chasing another bug related to the datadriven test thats blocking the backports (I think I just need to bump the version). I'll put out a fix for them.
Yes, we're not passing the `install.EnvOption{"COCKROACH_SCAN_MAX_IDLE_TIME=10ms"}` anymore which is likely why the test started to fail.

Nit: might be worth asserting that it maintains a strict descending order; it's not immediately obvious,

```
assert(len(upgradePath) == 1 || ugradePath[len(upgradePath)]-1] < chosenPredecessor
```

IMO, this invariant is part of the contract of the `releases` package (i.e., when you call `releases.LatestPredecessor`, you get an immediate predecessor). If we wanted to add an assertion, I'd rather assert ordering when loading the releases file (`parseReleases`).
Nm, since the order isn't required, maybe update the comment to say `...between _any_ two versions passed`.
Nit: we should update the comment for `mut.Generate` to say that the length of the resulting sequence is always even.
That is only true for the `preserveDowngradeOptionRandomizerMutator` implementation I think? Unless you meant just for that specific implementation, in which case I've added it.
We can ignore the error because both `FromVersion` and `ToVersion` are validated elsewhere?
